processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: multidirectionally hot forged in the temperature range 1123–1323 K

structures.overall_structure: Finer-grained austenite matrix with boundary ferrite (long parallel stripes / short thin laths) and fine deformation twins in austenite grains after forging; mean grain size 12.1 μm; ferrite area percentage 1.84%.

phases_present.morphology: matrix with fine grains, fine deformation twins and annealing twins
short thin ferrite laths / long parallel stripes at austenite grain boundaries

inclusions.name: AlN
inclusions.morphology: polyhedral with straight edges and sharp angles; some inclusions broken after forging

precipitates.distribution: number density 133 mm^-2; 84% of inclusions (mainly AlN) less than 2 μm; area ratio 1.005%

defect_interactions.interaction_type: AlN inclusion pinning of austenite grain boundaries
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Fine dispersed AlN inclusions acted as heterogeneous nucleation cores for austenite during solidification and pinned austenite grain boundaries, refining grains in the HN steel.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: Grain and twin boundaries hinder dislocation movement
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Many grain and twin boundaries in the HN steel hindered dislocation movement, indirectly promoting dislocation strengthening and enhancing strength and hardness.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Fine deformation twins and annealing twins in austenite grains promote uniform deformation; grain and twin boundaries hinder dislocation movement.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Nitrogen addition expanded the austenite phase field and reduced ferrite content (ferrite area 1.84% in HN); ferrite precipitated at austenite grain boundaries.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: round tensile specimen with Ø10 mm gauge section, 50 mm gauge length, overall length 114 mm (Figure 1a); Charpy-type impact specimen 10 mm × 10 mm × 50 mm with V-notch (Figure 1b)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: tensile speed 3 mm min^-1; tensile machine WDW-200; impact machine JB-300B

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: HN1/HN2/HN3 solid curves overlap during the elastic/plateau region peaking between 800 and 900 MPa and fracture at noticeably higher strain (~70–78%) than LN specimens.

service_conditions.stress_state: uniaxial tension (tensile test) and impact loading (Charpy V-notch test)

comparative_performance.improvement_percentage: UTS +9 MPa (841.5 vs 832.5 MPa); RA +13 percentage points (70 vs 57%); A +12 percentage points (74.5 vs 62.5%); CVN +49.5 J (130.5 vs 81 J); YS −38 MPa (647 vs 685 MPa)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: mechanical grinding followed by corrosion with 96 vol% alcohol + 4 vol% nitric acid
characterization_methods.purpose: reveal austenite/ferrite microstructure and measure grain size and ferrite area percentage
characterization_methods.key_findings: HN steel mean grain size 12.1 μm; ferrite area percentage 1.84%; finer grains and fine deformation twins in austenite grains after forging.
Main inclusion in HN steel was AlN with straight edge and sharp angle; AlN inclusions could be broken after forging.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SEM images from 50 random view fields at 500×
characterization_methods.purpose: measure number and size of inclusions
characterization_methods.key_findings: HN steel: number density 133 mm^-2, average size 1.521 μm, area ratio 1.005%; NP of inclusions <2 μm = 84%, NP <4 μm = 95%.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; strain rate 1×10^-3 s^-1; tensile speed 3 mm min^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: determine YS, UTS, RA, elongation and stress-strain curves

characterization_methods.technique: SEM and super-depth of field microscopy
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM and super-depth of field microscope (VHX-500)
characterization_methods.purpose: observe tensile and impact fracture morphologies
characterization_methods.key_findings: HN tensile fracture had a crater shape with larger, deeper and more uniformly distributed dimples; HN impact fracture dimples were larger, deeper and more uniform with higher shear-lip area ratio than LN.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Fe–28Mn–10Al–0.8C–N pseudobinary; temperature 700–1800 K; nitrogen mass fraction 0.0–2.0 wt%

computational_details.simulation_method: Thermodynamic calculation of liquidus and solidus

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Fe–28Mn–10Al–0.8C steels; [Al] 0–10 wt%; [N] 0.00–0.02 and 0.11–0.15 wt% (broken y-axis); smelting temperature 1873 K, liquidus 1587 K, solidus 1493 K
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: HN composition (Al 9.95 wt%, N 0.1326 wt%) lies far above the equilibrium AlN line at the smelting temperature, consistent with AlN inclusions being stable during smelting in HN steel.

unmapped_findings: Chemical composition of the HN steel (Table 1, wt%): Mn 28.10, Al 9.95, C 0.81, N 0.1326, S 0.0093, Fe Bal.
Impact energy (CVN) of the HN steel: 130.5(±5.5) J (Table 2).

The HN tensile fracture had a crater shape with larger, deeper and more uniformly distributed dimples than LN; the HN impact fracture showed larger, deeper and more uniform dimples with a higher shear-lip area ratio.
Aggregated AlN inclusions were detected in the dimples of the HN steel; they were generated during the smelting process and tended to cause crack initiation (detrimental to mechanical properties).

AlN stability diagram: the HN composition (Al 9.95 wt%, N 0.1326 wt%) lies far above the equilibrium AlN line at the smelting temperature (1873 K), so AlN inclusions can be easily formed and stably exist during smelting.
Liquidus (1587 K) and solidus (1493 K) of the investigated steel were calculated using FactSage 8.0.
Fracture toughness of the HN steel was distinctly enhanced by nitrogen addition (qualitative statement; no numeric fracture toughness value is reported).
